verses.text: But the Spirit says expressly that in later times some will fall away from the faith, paying attention to seducing spirits and doctrines of demons,
through the hypocrisy of men who speak lies, branded in their own conscience as with a hot iron;
forbidding marriage and commanding to abstain from foods which God created to be received with thanksgiving by those who believe and know the truth.
For every creature of God is good, and nothing is to be rejected, if it is received with thanksgiving.
For it is sanctified through the word of God and prayer.
If you instruct the brothers of these things, you will be a good servant of Christ Jesus, nourished in the words of the faith, and of the good doctrine which you have followed.
But refuse profane and old wives’ fables. Exercise yourself toward godliness.
For bodily exercise has some value, but godliness has value in all things, having the promise of the life which is now, and of that which is to come.
This saying is faithful and worthy of all acceptance.
For to this end we both labor and suffer reproach, because we have set our trust in the living God, who is the Savior of all men, especially of those who believe.
Let no man despise your youth; but be an example to those who believe, in word, in your way of life, in love, in spirit, in faith, and in purity.
Until I come, pay attention to reading, to exhortation, and to teaching.
Don’t neglect the gift that is in you, which was given to you by prophecy, with the laying on of the hands of the elders.
Be diligent in these things. Give yourself wholly to them, that your progress may be revealed to all.
Pay attention to yourself, and to your teaching. Continue in these things, for in doing this you will save both yourself and those who hear you.

footnotes.content: The Spirit warned this would happen — people would fall away, drawn by deceiving spirits. It shouldn't surprise us, but it should keep us rooted. Our hope isn't in a trend, it's in Jesus who never changes.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Lies repeated enough can sear a conscience until it goes numb. But God can still tenderize it again. His grace awakens what sin has dulled.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God gave marriage and food as good gifts to be received with thanksgiving. The problem isn't the gift, it's rejecting gifts the Giver made. Gratitude honors him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Everything God made is good. When we receive it with thankfulness, we see it as it is — a gift from a generous Father. Gratitude turns ordinary meals into worship.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God's word and prayer sanctify our gifts. We don't make them holy by our mood, but by receiving them as his. He meets us in the ordinary.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Teaching others these truths makes us good servants of Christ. We grow as we feed others. The nourishment we give away often feeds us too.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ignore silly tales and train yourself for godliness. Our culture trains us in many things, but few train us to love Jesus more. Choose your training wisely.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Exercise has value, but godliness profits forever. We care for our bodies, but our souls need daily training too. The best investment is time with the Lord.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: This is a saying worth staking our lives on. Godliness isn't a burden — it's a gift with promises for now and for eternity. We run toward it, not away from it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: We labor and suffer because our hope is in the living God, Savior of all — especially those who believe. He is worth it. On the hardest days, that hope holds.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Command and teach these things. Paul doesn't say 'suggest' — but he says it as a shepherd who loves. Truth spoken in love is mercy to those who need it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Don't let anyone look down on your youth. Be an example — in speech, life, love, faith, and purity. God often uses young hearts to revive old ones. Let your life speak.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Pay attention to reading Scripture, to exhortation, to teaching. Before Timothy does anything fancy, he's told to stay with the words of God. That's still our job.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Don't neglect the gift God gave you through prophecy and the laying on of hands. Gifts aren't for show — they're for serving. Use what he's given while you have it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Be diligent. Give yourself wholly to these things. Progress may be slow, but it will be seen. God delights to grow what we faithfully tend.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Watch your life and your teaching closely. Your faithfulness helps save both you and those who hear. It's sobering, but it's also an invitation to stay near Jesus.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
